raw_response:
I am old now, and with only 2 mu, I do not farm like big households. I still plant cotton on all my land because I know this crop and I have done it many years. Cotton gives me trouble with picking, but I understand its temper. If I change to something else, I am not steady in my heart. Some people in the family work outside, so labor at home is not always enough. Because of that, I keep things simple and do what has worked on my field before.

This year I will plant cotton around mid to late April, after the जमीन warms up well. I will use the cotton seed we usually buy from the local dealer, not the most expensive kind, just the kind people nearby also use. I will put some fertilizer before planting, not too little, because if cotton starts weak it is hard to catch up later. But I also cannot spend too much money at once, so I will split it: one part as base fertilizer, one part later when the plants are growing well. I have a well, so if spring is dry I will irrigate once after planting or after seedlings come up badly, then again around flowering if the soil is too dry. Water costs money, so I will not water just for peace of mind if there has already been decent rain. For pests, I do not spray on schedule like a factory farm. I look first. If I see insects or too much grass, then I spend the money. For tillage I will use the usual simple plowing and ridging before planting. Harvest will be by hand in several pickings, as always. I do not expect a huge yield, just a steady one that matches my small land and old age.
